newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas slips again, winter under most pressure.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas slips again, winter under most pressure.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market continued to fall on Friday, adding further to the losses seen in the morning session.
The volumes traded were higher than in recent days, with a total of 205 lots transacted, 150 of these done in January and February, which came under the greatest pressure.

Both these months settled at 15.80 pence a therm, a loss of a full 0.50 pence a therm over the day. But every other month also fell, with both April (9.45 pence) and September (9.90 pence) trading at contract lows.

"There's been heavy pressure on the sell side on winter,", a broker said. He added that the summer had dipped on the OTC market but then bounced back, but there had continued to be quite a lot of pressure on winter.

Trade was seen in April, July, August and September as well as in the winter, but volumes in the nearer months were small. The futures market was seen as driven by the OTC market, which also fell significantly over the day.
